hey i would love for there to be improved integration of posthog into the product at different surfaces from funnels to the ai at different turns durations and posthogs various libraries. I want you to go all in, think of surveys you could add, think of all this stuff. here is some things post hog said could be improved as well: Here's the full picture from the first 36 hours of 3.0.0.

---

The quick summary

7 users started a session since launch. Remember: tracking may be undercounting, and some users block tracking entirely.

The funnel story

The biggest problem isn't the product — it's getting people into it. Of 16 visitors:

- 69% bounced without clicking "Start session" — this is your sharpest drop and the one worth fixing first
- 67% of people who started a session never sent a message — once users get in, something is blocking them from engaging

Everyone who sent a message got a response, so the core AI pipeline is healthy.

Feature adoption

Model switching is the standout feature — the majority of post-launch users changed models. Everything else (quiz, speech, session sharing, forking) has zero or near-zero usage. Those either need better discovery or more time.

Errors

Launch day had 4 error types: auth, invalid-request, model-unavailable, and unknown. The auth one is concerning — it could mean real users hit a wall when trying to authenticate.

---

Agent turn gaps to close (your specific ask)

Your agent_turn_completed event fires, but you're missing the full lifecycle:

Gap | Fix
No agent_turn_started | Add this — without it you can't measure latency or detect stuck turns
No model property | Add to agent_turn_completed and message_sent
No duration_ms | Measure from turn start to completion
No success/error flag | Can't distinguish clean turns from failed ones
No from_model/to_model on model_changed | Your most-used feature is completely opaque

The single highest-leverage fix: add agent_turn_started + duration_ms + model + success. That alone would make your most critical event actually useful for debugging and performance monitoring.

Also worth doing: add an app_version property to all events — without it you can't cleanly compare 3.0.0 vs future releases.

If you want to save this report as a permanent notebook, hit "Create notebook" in the UI above.

I’m mapping the actual identity, analytics, routing, and reusable UI paths. I’m also applying the Impeccable interface guidance because the survey/first-run placement is part of the requested product polish; I’ll keep this strictly read-only.

content.text:
Read-only integration map complete; no files changed.

The sharpest activation finding is the full-screen `ChatIntro` gate before the `/chat` composer. Users must click a second “[ GET STARTED ]” before seeing the already-strong `SuggestedPrompts` experience. Removing that gate and opening directly on composer plus starter prompts is the clearest response to the 67% session-without-message drop.

Other key findings:

- Keating has no general product account. Provider OAuth is local credential authorization, not Keating identity. Keep PostHog anonymous; use chat session UUID only as an event property. Identify only if a future global server-validated product account is available, resetting on logout.
- Current source already sends `from_model` and `to_model` for `model_changed`; the PostHog report reflects an older deployment or capture gap.
- Pi already exposes the complete lifecycle needed for run duration, provider-turn duration, TTFT, tool latency, model/provider, token usage, cost, stop reason, and success. Instrument `agent_start/end`, `turn_start/end`, `message_start/update/end`, and tool execution events rather than treating `agent_end` as one agent turn.
- Several existing events disclose content contrary to the privacy page: prompt text, session-derived topics, quiz topics, and raw OAuth errors. A central sanitizer should remove content, secrets, dynamic route IDs, query strings, and raw errors.
- Session replay should default off. The in-progress configuration defaults it on whenever `VITE_POSTHOG_SESSION_REPLAY` is undefined, and Docker does not currently provide that build argument.
- SPA pageviews should use `capture_pageview: "history_change"`. The `/ingest` proxies can support flags, surveys, and tours, but are hardcoded to the US endpoints regardless of `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST`.
- Exception tracking will need hidden sourcemap upload for useful production stacks; Vite currently disables sourcemaps.

Recommended survey sequence:

1. Landing friction survey after meaningful dwell or desktop exit intent.
2. Inline activation-blocker survey after 30–60 seconds with a visible composer and zero messages.
3. Existing thumbs or a PostHog thumb survey after the first or third successful response.
4. One-shot auth recovery survey following an auth error and successful retry.
5. Sampled quiz usefulness/difficulty question.
6. PMF survey after several successful sessions or sufficient tenure.

Use fixed choices with immediate recovery actions. Reserve free text for explicit opt-in because it becomes learner content held by PostHog. Low-adoption features are better introduced by one contextual, feature-flagged tip at a time than by a modal tour.

Suggested tests include PostHog initialization/privacy behavior, exact agent-event sequence timing, replay-off default, onboarding eligibility and cooldowns, OAuth error categorization, dynamic-route sanitization, responsive survey stories, and a real Vite/Nitro `/ingest` browser smoke test.
